01 / THE DENOMINATOR MATTERS

A larger fare does not settle the decision.

Base fare per trip

Mean fare_amount. USD, excluding tips and added charges.

Base fare per occupied hour

Total base fare ÷ total occupied minutes × 60. USD/hour.

These are pooled rates, not averages of individual trip rates. Occupied time excludes queues, idle time and repositioning. This metric is not driver earnings or profit.

02 / THE MISSING MINUTES

Make the waiting-time assumption visible.

Trip records do not contain a vehicle’s queue, idle or repositioning time. Change the assumed minutes to see when the comparison reverses.

ASSUMPTIONS / NOT OBSERVED IN THE DATA

Extra time per completed trip

Each assumption bundles queue, idle and repositioning time. It is applied once per trip. Both airports share the airport assumption so the comparison is transparent.

Base fare per modeled cycle hour = total base fare ÷ (occupied minutes + trips × assumed extra minutes) × 60.

SCENARIO OUTPUT / USD PER MODELED CYCLE HOUR

How much extra airport time can the fare absorb?

Threshold where airport base fare per modeled cycle hour equals the Manhattan benchmark, given the selected city-time assumption. This is an algebraic comparison, not a measured operational limit.

03 / CHECK THE NEXT MONTH

Freeze the ranking. Then open April.

January–March determines the preferred route by occupied-hour productivity. April checks whether that descriptive ordering persists.

Population and exclusions

One source row represents one reported taxi trip. Primary eligibility requires pickup within its source month, positive occupied duration from 1 to 180 minutes, distance greater than 0 and at most 100 miles, base fare greater than 0 and at most $500, card/cash payment, standard/JFK rate, and valid mapped locations.

What is included in the rate?

The numerator is fare_amount only. Tips, tolls, taxes, airport fees, other surcharges and the 2025 CBD congestion fee are excluded. Total passenger charges are not treated as operator revenue. Cash tips are absent from the source, so tipping is not used for route ranking.

What does the holdout prove?

It checks the persistence of a descriptive ranking in a later month. It does not estimate the causal effect of dispatching more taxis to an airport. Airport queues, vehicle availability, driver costs and foregone trips are missing. One holdout month does not establish seasonal stability.

Source, terms and reproducibility

Source: NYC Taxi & Limousine Commission trip records and its Yellow Taxi data dictionary. TLC notes that the data come from technology providers and does not guarantee accuracy. See NYC Open Data terms.

The project includes SQL, Python, a notebook, tests, a data dictionary, file hashes and source download instructions. Raw trip files are downloaded separately. This study has no affiliation with NYC TLC.
